feed.title: Data Science & ML — Useful Sites
feed.subtitle: A hand-curated, annotated link directory across ten areas, from software and AI to security, economics and architecture. Every entry states what the resource does and where it parts ways with its neighbours.

entry.title: CIA World Factbook
entry.summary: A reference giving geography, population, economy, government and military indicators for every country on uniform pages; public domain. Unlike Wikipedia country articles every country has the same fields in the same order, which makes comparison easy. The publisher is an intelligence agency — keep that in mind for interpretive fields.

entry.title: Data Commons
entry.summary: A Google-backed project that merges statistics from the Census, WHO, the UN and dozens of other sources into one knowledge graph, queryable in natural language and through an API. Unlike single-agency portals it sets series from different sources side by side in one query. Google’s old Public Data Explorer address redirects here.

entry.title: Google Cloud Public Datasets
entry.summary: Public datasets that live inside BigQuery: GitHub, Wikipedia, weather, the census. Unlike the AWS Open Data Registry the data comes as tables you query with SQL rather than files; within the monthly free query quota you can work without downloading.

entry.title: Google Trends
entry.summary: A tool showing how search interest changes over time and place. Unlike keyword planners it gives a relative 0–100 index rather than absolute search counts; useful for gauging public interest, seasonality and rising topics.

entry.title: NASA Earthdata
entry.summary: NASA’s portal to its satellite and Earth-observation data, from rainfall and ice cover to vegetation and the atmosphere. Unlike NOAA’s ground-station records it rests on measurements taken from space; downloads need a free Earthdata account.

entry.title: NOAA NCEI
entry.summary: The US national archive of weather, climate, ocean and geophysical data, formerly NCDC. Unlike NASA Earthdata it holds decades-long series of station and observation records rather than imagery — the primary source for past weather.

entry.title: OpenCorporates
entry.summary: One of the largest open databases of companies, merging national company registers into one search. Unlike individual national registers it presents many jurisdictions in the same form; officer and affiliate links make it useful for investigation, while heavy API use is paid.

entry.title: r/datasets
entry.summary: A community for finding and requesting datasets. Unlike catalogue sites you can post a request when the data you want is missing and see what others have found; there is no quality control, so check the licence and source yourself.

entry.title: UCI Machine Learning Repository
entry.summary: One of the oldest archives for machine-learning research, home to classic small sets such as Iris and Adult. Unlike Kaggle it is an academic archive rather than a contest site: each set comes with its donor, field descriptions and citation, and papers use them as benchmarks.

entry.title: UNdata
entry.summary: A data service pulling the statistics of UN bodies into one search: population, agriculture, energy, trade, education. Unlike visiting each agency’s site it builds country-by-year comparison tables; for depth, the source agency’s own portal is better.

entry.title: Uppsala Conflict Data Program
entry.summary: Uppsala University’s data programme on armed conflict and organised violence, keeping event-level records with coordinates. Unlike news archives each event is verified against coding rules; it is a standard reference in conflict research.

entry.title: WHO Global Health Observatory
entry.summary: The World Health Organization’s country-level health indicators: causes of death, vaccination, health spending, risk factors. Unlike national health agencies’ figures, it puts countries on the same definitions and methods so they can be compared; the data is also available through an API.

entry.title: Awesome ArcGIS Developer
entry.summary: Developer resources for ArcGIS, the mapping and location-analysis platform. Unlike open-source GIS lists, it centres on the commercial Esri ecosystem, and Esri maintains it.

entry.title: Awesome Core ML Models
entry.summary: A list of ready machine-learning models for Apple’s Core ML framework. Unlike general model hubs, every model is already in Core ML format for on-device use on iOS/macOS; part of the list is dated.

entry.title: Awesome CSV
entry.summary: A list of tools and resources for CSV, the tabular-data file format. Unlike strictly schema’d formats (Parquet, JSON Schema) CSV is loose, and the list gathers the command-line tools and libraries that cope with its quirks.

entry.title: Awesome Deep Learning
entry.summary: A list of courses, papers, frameworks and datasets for deep learning. Unlike general ML lists it focuses on neural networks and modern architectures.

entry.title: Awesome Deep Learning Papers
entry.summary: A list compiling the most-cited deep-learning papers of 2012–2016; it is no longer maintained. Unlike live trackers such as Papers with Code, it offers a fixed core chosen by citation count — a historical entry point to the field’s foundations.

entry.title: Awesome H2O
entry.summary: A list for H2O, the open-source distributed machine-learning platform. Unlike scikit-learn, it runs distributed across a cluster and has AutoML built in.

entry.title: Awesome JAX
entry.summary: A list for JAX, which offers automatic differentiation and XLA compilation. Unlike PyTorch it is functional: you apply transformations such as grad, jit and vmap to pure functions.

entry.title: Awesome JSON
entry.summary: A list of tools and resources for JSON, the text-based data-interchange format. Unlike a single parser, it brings together schema validators, query tools such as jq and libraries per language.

entry.title: Awesome Jupyter
entry.summary: A resource list for Jupyter notebooks, which hold code, text and charts together. Unlike the Jupyter docs, it gathers the ecosystem around it — extensions, kernels, tools that turn a notebook into an app or slides.

entry.title: Awesome NLG
entry.summary: A list for generating text from data or dialogue (natural-language generation). Unlike general NLP lists it is about producing text rather than understanding it; much of it predates large language models.

entry.title: Awesome OpenStreetMap
entry.summary: A list of tools and resources for OpenStreetMap, the open map-data project. Unlike the Google Maps API the data is openly licensed (ODbL) and fully downloadable; the list gathers editors, processors and renderers.

entry.title: Awesome Public Datasets
entry.summary: A list of public datasets organised by topic. Unlike random data search it points to clean, usable sources grouped by domain.

entry.title: Awesome Python Data Science
entry.summary: A list organising Python data-science libraries by workflow (data, models, visualisation). Unlike a PyPI search it shows curated tools for each stage.

entry.title: Awesome Question Answering
entry.summary: A list for asking and answering questions in natural language (QA). Unlike general NLP lists, it focuses only on question answering — datasets, models, papers.

entry.title: Awesome R
entry.summary: A list of packages and resources for R, the statistics language. Unlike CRAN it foregrounds packages chosen by task (visualisation, machine learning).

entry.title: Awesome SE for ML
entry.summary: Resources for machine-learning engineering from experiment to production. Unlike model lists it looks at the “making ML a product” side — testing, deployment, monitoring.

entry.title: Awesome TensorFlow
entry.summary: A list of resources and models for TensorFlow, the machine-intelligence library. Unlike the official docs, it gathers community tutorials, models and projects; part of it dates from the TensorFlow 1 era.

entry.title: AWS Open Data Registry
entry.summary: A registry of large public datasets hosted on AWS. Unlike portals such as Data.gov the data sits directly in S3, so you can process it inside AWS without downloading.

entry.title: data.europa.eu
entry.summary: The European Union’s official open-data portal. Unlike national portals, it merges member states’ datasets into one search and also includes data from the EU institutions themselves.

entry.title: Data.gov
entry.summary: The US government’s open-data portal — canonical federal datasets. Unlike third-party compilations it is the official source; most records point on to the publishing agency’s site.

entry.title: DataHub
entry.summary: Curated open datasets in ready CSV/JSON form, plus tooling. Unlike raw portal data, they are cleaned and published as standard Frictionless Data packages.

entry.title: Figshare
entry.summary: A platform for sharing research outputs and datasets in citable form with DOIs. Compared with Zenodo it is a commercial product (Digital Science), also sold to universities as an institutional repository.

entry.title: Gapminder
entry.summary: Tools from the foundation Hans Rosling co-founded, presenting global development data through fact-based visualisations. Unlike raw data portals, it tells the data through charts moving over time, aimed at correcting common misconceptions.

entry.title: Humanitarian Data Exchange
entry.summary: Crisis and humanitarian datasets curated by OCHA. Unlike general open-data portals, it focuses on crisis areas, with data coming from organisations in the field.

entry.title: Opendatasoft
entry.summary: A platform institutions and cities use to run data portals, with datasets searchable across portals. Rather than visiting portals one by one, you can search the data of every portal built on it together.

entry.title: re3data
entry.summary: A registry of research-data repositories. Unlike general search engines, it classifies repositories by discipline, access terms, licence and certification — for choosing where to deposit your data.

entry.title: Zenodo
entry.summary: A CERN-backed open research repository that mints DOIs for datasets and software. Unlike Figshare it is non-profit, and it can automatically archive and DOI your GitHub releases.

entry.title: Academic Torrents
entry.summary: A community archive distributing large research datasets over BitTorrent. Against institutional download links the difference is durability: when the university server goes away, the data survives in the swarm.
